name: Essentialism
description: Essentialism treats a social category as if it reflects a deep, fixed, natural essence rather than a contingent or socially constructed grouping. Once a category feels natural and immutable, within-group variation gets easier to ignore.
design_relevance_note: Relevant to demographic segmentation, persona creation, onboarding defaults, fairness work, taxonomy design, and ML labeling. Essentialist category thinking can make teams treat flexible social identities as fixed design facts.
prevalence_note: Recognizable in inclusive-design, fairness, HCI-ethics, and social-cognition-adjacent research discussions, but still uncommon as a named concept in routine mainstream product-design critique.

findings.description: Review evidence indicates that people often represent human categories essentialistically, treating category boundaries as reflections of deep natural essences. This mode of thinking has consequential effects on how people perceive, evaluate, and interact with members of social groups.
